title: Interchange Fee Settlement Summary
description:
Helix Payments is a payment network. One of their products is an interchange fee summary of all the merchants in a country and mode of card transaction.

Interchange is the fee on an approved card payment. The rate depends on merchant category (`mcc`), country (`country_code`), and how the card was presented (`entry_mode` — chip, swipe, or contactless). Each rate is valid only between `effective_from` and `effective_to`.

Only approved payments (`response_code == "00"`) are in scope. Each of those payments must be priced with the rate that matches `(mcc, country_code, entry_mode)` and whose window contains the payment date:

```
interchange_fee = round(amount * rate_bps / 10000 + fixed_fee, 2)
```

Approved payments with no matching rate are out of scope. Helix cannot publish a fee without a rate.

**Run** uses a 20,000-row sample and a pruned rate card so you can check the CSV quickly. **Submit** uses the shared 100 million payment drop.

The output is one row per `(country_code, entry_mode)`:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `txn_count` | How many payments were priced in the group |
| `total_fee` | Sum of `interchange_fee` in the group |
| `distinct_rate_versions_used` | How many distinct `rate_id`s were used in the group |

data.overview: Helix Payments publishes an interchange fee summary by country and card presentment. Two Parquet drops: 100 million card payments (~3.60 GB) and a 682,500-row interchange rate card (~11.9 MB). Price approved payments with the rate that was in effect on the payment date. Run uses a 20,000-row sample and a pruned rate card; Submit uses the full drops.

datasets.name: Transactions
datasets.distribution: 100 million authorization rows over roughly half a year. Approvals dominate: 88 million of 100 million. One (MCC, country, entry mode) combination — grocery in the US on chip (5411, US, chip) — is 66 million of those approvals (75%), about 909× the next key. The other 5,250 keys sit around a median of ~1.6k rows. Joins and aggregations that hash on that composite key send a single task the majority of the work.

datasets.name: Interchange rate card
datasets.distribution: Weekly effective schedules per (MCC, country, entry mode) spanning a couple of years. 682,500 versioned rows — 11.9 MB on disk, large enough that Spark will not auto-broadcast it at the default 10 MB threshold. Windows are adjacent weeks, not overlapping.

expectedOutput.description: Distinct rate_id applied in the group (BIGINT)

gradeChecks: Spark job succeeds on the shared 100M drop
OUTPUT_PATH is a CSV directory with a header
grade/grade.py compares candidate CSV to the reference settlement summary

knobs.label: Shuffle partitions
knobs.help: Partitions used for shuffle exchanges (joins and aggregations).
